Reading the test class and `contains` is sufficient here because the question is specifically about the loop-header state at line 142 across all 21 tests.

From `src/cfnlint/jsonschema/_keywords.py`:
- `matches` starts at `0` before the loop.
- `max_contains = schema.get("maxContains", len(instance))`.
- At line 142, `for each in instance:` begins each iteration.
- Inside the body, `matches` is incremented only if `contains_validator.is_valid(each)`.
- The early exit happens only after increment, and only when `matches > max_contains`.

So at any later loop-header event, `matches` can equal the number of previously seen matching items, and because the function only returns on `matches > max_contains`, it is entirely possible for execution to reach the next loop header with `matches == max_contains`. That already disproves the candidate invariant `matches < max_contains`.

The tests in `files/tests/qa/testcase.py` include several concrete cases where this equality must occur before another iteration:
- `test_max_contains_2_array_3_integers`: after processing `1` and `2`, `matches == 2` and `maxContains == 2`; the loop still proceeds to the third item, so the next line-142 event occurs with `matches == max_contains`.
- `test_max_contains_1_array_2_strings`: after the first string, `matches == 1` with `maxContains == 1`, then the second iteration begins.
- `test_max_contains_3_array_4_integers`, `test_contains_dict_schema_overshoot`, `test_contains_with_array_subschema_overshoot`, and others have the same structure.
- Even some no-overshoot runs can hit equality at the final iteration boundary only if another iteration follows; but the overshoot tests are enough to show the invariant fails.

Therefore the invariant is not always true at every line-142 event.
